title: NHM HMS Challenger sediment/preparation collection: diagnostic object-level harvest and address crosswalk

official_resource.dataset: Listing of HMS Challenger Sediment Collection
official_resource.resource: Sir John Murray's Challenger Sediment Collection

count_states.rule: Preserve these as different dated catalogue/documentary states. Do not silently normalize one to the other.

official_resource.resource_metadata_note: The portal currently describes the resource with XLSX media type while also exposing 'CSV' format labels in resource metadata. Treat the downloadable file format as a versioned portal property rather than a historical collection fact.

registration_address_rule.M_prefix: Museum-added Murray Collection registration namespace after transfer into BM(NH)/NHM custody.
registration_address_rule.base_plus_bracket: M base number generally groups material from a sampling site; bracketed subnumber addresses an individual object/preparation within that base record.
non_bijective_examples: M.120 represents material from Challenger Stations 95 and 96.
registration_address_rule.interpretation: Station ↔ M number is a crosswalk, not a guaranteed one-to-one identity.

diagnostic_preparation_records.object_type: wooden cavity slide with loose sediment

diagnostic_preparation_records.preparator_or_annotation: made in Göttingen by Voigt & Hochgesang / firm attribution in published collection history

diagnostic_preparation_records.object_type: wooden cavity slide with fragments of nodules
diagnostic_preparation_records.grade: A; bracketed subnumber unresolved in available text

diagnostic_preparation_records.object_type: open / thickly cut section of nodule

specialist_return_event.route: returned to the British Museum through Dr A. Schoep, University of Ghent
specialist_return_event.interpretation: The collection includes later specialist working subsets that returned to museum custody; this is not simply an untouched shipboard sediment archive.
specialist_return_event.guard: Published historical reconstruction associates this group with Renard-linked work, but a direct publication-to-each-slide crosswalk remains open.

physical_storage.slide_cabinet: 105-drawer cabinet stored separately from the main sediment collection at South Kensington
formats: sediment embedded in resin and sectioned
thin sections of nodules and rocks
physical_storage.payoff: A single historical sample can acquire multiple physical and documentary derivatives, so object form must be harvested alongside station and registration address.

row_harvest_limit.problem: The official resource is downloadable but no datastore table/view is exposed on the resource page, and the binary resource could not be retrieved in this runtime. Therefore this file does not claim a complete 4,723-row spreadsheet harvest.
row_harvest_limit.completed_instead: Object-level records and field architecture explicitly exposed in the official resource documentation and accompanying published collection study were harvested as a diagnostic layer.
next_when_binary_available: Load every row without early exit.
Subset records whose object/container/preparation wording indicates slide, preparation, thin section, strew, cavity or mounted material.
Search all free-text columns for Haeckel, Norman, Voigt, Hochgesang, Schoep, Renard and other named preparators/annotators.
Preserve M base and bracketed subnumber separately.
Build station → M base → item → preparation-form → specialist → publication fields.

research_payoff: The Challenger material now demonstrates a genuinely non-bijective address system. Field station numbers, museum M registrations and preparation subnumbers overlap without collapsing into one namespace. Named preparations by Haeckel, Norman and Voigt/Hochgesang make the slide cabinet a history of specialist interventions rather than merely a storage residue.
